subject: Clarifying SLAs and emergency rewrap procedure for KMS operator events
messages:
From: Asha Rao <security@polariscorp.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: operator change-log + emergency rewrap runbook for SOC2 evidence

Hi Priya,

Following up on our checklist for the SOC 2 readiness review next month. Can you please provide the following items related to your KMS/HSM operations for tenant-scoped keys?

1) Operator change-log (last 12 months) filtered to actions that affected key state (create, wrap, unwrap, rotate, revoke). Ideally CSV with timestamp, operator id, action, key-id, and a short reason.
2) The current emergency rewrap procedure and SLA commitments when a key custody event triggers an on-call ceremony (we need: expected RTO for rollback, who can approve, and post-incident evidence steps).
3) A short summary of controls that prevent single-operator wrap/unwrap (dual control, split knowledge, or automation safeguards).

We'd like to ingest the files into our audit portal by Apr 6. If any of this is sensitive and requires an NDA or secure transfer, tell me the preferred channel.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turn.

Asha Rao
Senior Security Engineer
Polaris Corp
security@polariscorp.com
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <security@polariscorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operator change-log + emergency rewrap runbook for SOC2 evidence

Hi Asha —

Thanks for the checklist. We can provide everything you listed. Quick notes up front so expectations are aligned:

- Operator change-log: we can export the operator audit stream for the last 12 months as a CSV. It will include operator id (internal SSO), action type, key alias (tenant-prefixed), and a short action reason. We will redact raw key material.
- Emergency rewrap runbook: we will share the current runbook (v1.3) and include the SLA table for canary, regular, and emergency rewraps.
- Dual-control: Redwood enforces split-knowledge for rewrap ceremonies for customer-managed KEKs; for hosted tenant keys we use automated rewraps gated by an approval flow (two approvers) + time-based holds.

I'll coordinate the export and attach the CSV + runbook. Ben, Marissa — please pull the operator CSV and canonical runbook. Jonas — can you confirm retention slice and whether we need to provide operator SSO mapping for Polaris?

Asha — we will share via a pre-authenticated signed drive link and also can SFTP if you prefer. Let me know which you want.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Asha Rao <security@polariscorp.com>

Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 11:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operator change-log + emergency rewrap runbook for SOC2 evidence

Priya / Asha — attaching the exports here (stubs attached below).

Attachment stubs:
- redwood-kms-operator-transcripts-20280327.csv (CSV, 412 KB) — columns: timestamp_utc, operator_sso, action, key_alias, tenant_id, reason, request_id
- rotation-governance-runbook-v1.3.pdf (PDF, 78 KB) — includes SLA matrix and approval flow diagrams
- key-eviction-audit-sample.txt (TXT, 20 KB) — sample of automated eviction event and webhook proof-of-acknowledgement

Summary of salient points from the runbook:
- Emergency rewrap SLA: target RTO 2 hours (critical) when both hardware and network are available; 8 hours under degraded modes with manual operator ceremony.
- Approval model: two distinct approvers required for customer-key rewraps (from the authorization queue) — either two humans or a human + automated verifier service.
- Logs: operator actions are immutably recorded in the audit stream and shipped to an append-only bucket with WORM retention for 90 days (longer retention available under enterprise contracts).

Jonas — retention mapping: we include operator SSO -> employee email in the separate mapping; we'll provide as a sanitized table (no PII) unless Polaris requires full IDs. 

Asha — preferred delivery is a signed drive link; I will create it and send a secure link + one-time password.

Ben Carter
Security & Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference
